items.title: Dawoud Sabu Adeyola interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 30, 2025
items.q: You know Benny & the Jets and James Brown and the Cadillacs and all these old people. So we grew up on doo-wop basically.

ctx.x: Be careful what you ask for — what you pray for, you know, ‘cause it may come back to haunt you. Because I was never at home. But no, yeah, we were very much affect— and see the other thing about those days is that there was only a couple of radio stations and you had race record stores and you had what they called race records — I mean radio stations. And so we were all in the ‘50s pretty much listening to the same music, you know, the popular music of the time you know. We knew as much about the black R&B…

forms of blues. And so I guess we started out imitating those sounds and those chords on the piano, which is a lot of repetition. [scats] So we kind of taught ourselves how to — nobody ever really taught us how to do that, we kind of figured it out.
